newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda denies supporting Zairean rebels.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda denies supporting Zairean rebels.

text.p: President Pasteur Bizimungu on Monday denied that Rwanda was providing military help to Tutsi rebels in eastern Zaire but said he morally supported their struggle against "extermination" by Zairean authorities.
Bizimungu also denied that Rwanda's Tutsi-dominated army had been involved in the shelling of Rwandan Hutu refugee camps in eastern Zaire.

"We are not supporting the Banyamulenge military. We are not interested in the conquest of land, but people's rights must be respected. The Banyamulenge are entitled to live in Zaire," the president told a news conference at his Kigali office.
"Morally I support their struggle between extermination and survival, I support their resistance against the Zairean authories."
The Banyamulenge are ethnic Tutsis who migrated to what is now Zaire up to two centuries ago.
They have been fighting Zairean troops for nearly two weeks after Zairean authorities threatened to expel them.

Their position in Zaire has been complicated by the arrival in the country two years ago of more than one million Rwandan Hutus, some of whom took part in the 1994 Rwandan genocide of up to one million Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
Denying charges his forces shelled the camps, Bizimungu said: "We do not have the weaponry to shell the camps from our positions."

Bizimungu said he had heard rumours of French military deployment in eastern Zaire, but thought such a development unlikely. France denied on Monday that it had sent any troops to Zaire or intended to.

Bizimungu said: "I don't see the reason or motivation because France has been silent when the Banyamulenge have been persecuted by the Zaireans and intervention by the French now would only be equal to what they did in 1994 when they watched as the Tutsis were being massacred in Rwanda."
Bizimungu, himself a Hutu, accused Zaire of being the trouble maker in the Great Lakes region: "Zaire has allowed traffic of arms in the refugee camps, it has armed and trained the refugees."
Asked if he would consider supporting the Banyamulenge if they faced extermination he said: "Should we reach that level then we shall consider."
